channel.title: Eastern Daily Press - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Eastern Daily Press (edp24.co.uk)

item.title: Fears park homes site could be sold off for redevelopment
item.description: People living on a residential park in King's Lynn fear it could be bought by a developer if the council puts it up for sale.

item.title: Thai restaurant shuts its doors in the city
item.description: A Thai restaurant in Exchange Street is closing its doors until January 28 and will launch a new menu when it reopens.

item.title: New shop to open in city after council gives plans the green light
item.description: An application to change the use of a building on Aylsham Road from an accountant firm to a charity shop has been approved.

item.title: Study carried out at the UEA reveals evidence that ‘nurses do save lives'
item.description: Study carried out at the University of East Anglia (UEA) in Norwich finds evidence that "nurses do save lives".

item.title: Mum-of-four stepping back from family-run florist near the city
item.description: Vicky Daniels, the manager at Buds 2 Bloom in New Costessey, has stepped back from the business after nearly 16 years.

item.title: Discover dementia-friendly activities in Norfolk and Suffolk
item.description: A search of the internet reveals many activities that would entertain and invigorate older people and especially those with some form of cognitive decline. Here are some of them...

item.title: Church refused restoration work over fears graves would be disturbed
item.description: Planners for Norwich City Council have turned down plans to build an access point and restore walls at the Congregational Church on Colegate in Norwich.

item.title: Firm which made masks for hit zombie film plans to create humanoid robot skin
item.description: AnthroTek, in Victoria Way, Studlands Industrial Estate, was selected for Startups 100 Index 2026, having recently worked on 28 Years Later.

item.title: Toxic mould cause of castle dungeon closure
item.description: Museum bosses have revealed toxic mould is the reason castle dungeons are off limits to visitors — but they are to reopen soon.

item.title: Almost 150 people BANNED from Norfolk's tips and libraries over shocking behaviour
item.description: Nearly 150 people have been banned from Norfolk's tips and libraries for violent threats to staff, abusive behaviour and harassment.
